newsitem.title: USA: NBC says won't join new TV rating system.
newsitem.headline: NBC says won't join new TV rating system.

text.p: General Electric Co's National Broadcasting Co Inc unit said it will not participate in the revised voluntary TV ratings system.

The other major U.S. networks as well as cable broadcasters agreed to modify the current age-based ratings system to better identify program content, U.S. Sen. John McCain, an Arizona Republican, announced on Wednesday.

NBC, in a statement late Wednesday, said it will not be part of the new agreement. "NBC is disappointed that the industry capitulated to political and special interest pressure and did not look more seriously at the implications of the flawed process in which they engaged," NBC said.

The network said it was concerned that "the ultimate aim of the current system's critics is to dictate programming content...there is no place for government involvement in what people watch on television."

Walt Disney Co's ABC, Westinghouse Electric Corp's CBS, and News Corp Ltd's Fox agreed to the new system, which will add content ratings to the existing age-based ratings, including the letters S for sex, L for language, V for violence, and D for suggestive dialogue. The new system is to take effect on Oct 1.
